claim_reference: Adv. Funct. Mater. 2026, 36:e75639, SI Section 7, Table S6, Figure S9

preregistration.hypothesis: Random 5-fold CV accurately estimates prospective active learning generalization, and high overall R^2 indicates high fidelity across all tissue targets.
preregistration.primary_metric: Comparison of Random 5-fold R^2 vs Forward-Chaining / LOCO R^2, and soft-regime subset R^2 (E < 3 kPa).
preregistration.decision_rule: SUPPORTED if Forward-Chaining R^2 matches Random CV R^2 within 0.05 and soft-regime R^2 >= 0.70; WEAKENED if soft-regime R^2 collapses (< 0.20 or negative) despite high overall R^2 (Simpson's paradox / range restriction) or selection leakage is confirmed; CONTRADICTED if LOCO R^2 < 0.0.

selection_leakage_finding.finding: Selection leakage detected in SI Section 7 digital twin benchmarking
selection_leakage_finding.description: Upstream digital_twin.py performed a single 80/20 train/test split with random_state=30. Bayesian optimization of hyperparameters was conducted on the 80% split, but final model architecture selection (GB vs SVR vs GP) and Table S6 performance claims were evaluated and chosen directly on the 20% test partition without an independent external test holdout.
selection_leakage_finding.consequence: Reported R^2 values in Table S6 (GB R^2=0.90, SVR R^2=0.92) reflect post-hoc selection over test performance rather than strictly out-of-sample generalization.

summary: Cross-validation estimand audit demonstrates severe range restriction (Simpson's paradox): while Random 5-Fold achieves an overall R^2 of 0.76, the subset R^2 in the soft regime (E < 3 kPa) collapses to -2.93, with soft RMSE (1.44 kPa) exceeding the target window by 9.6x. Under Leave-One-Campaign-Out (LOCO), R^2 drops to 0.63. Furthermore, nearest-neighbor KS test (stat = 0.732, p < 1e-10) confirms non-uniform input clustering, and SI Section 7 exhibits test set selection leakage.
